approachQuestion.prompt:
Universal two-way contact. A directed network is supplied as a V by V boolean adjacency matrix M, where M[u][v] is true exactly when u can send directly to v. Return true exactly when every vertex can reach every other vertex through zero or more directed edges. Return false otherwise.

The matrix is read-only; 1 <= V <= 2000, with a false diagonal. No adjacency lists are supplied. All matrix cells can be accessed in constant time. Output one boolean.

Example 1: M=[[false,true,false],[false,false,true],[true,false,false]], output=true.
Example 2: M=[[false,true],[false,false]], output=false.
Example 3: M=[[false]], output=true.

options.text: From vertex 0, traverse using matrix rows and check that every vertex is reached. Then traverse from 0 using matrix columns as reverse edges and check that every vertex is reached. Return true only when both checks pass.
options.feedback: The first search proves 0 can reach everyone, and the reverse search proves everyone can reach 0. Combining these routes proves reachability for every ordered pair. Row/column access uses the supplied matrix directly.

options.text: Use two queue traversals from 0, first scanning rows for outgoing neighbors and then columns for incoming neighbors. Return true only if both traversals reach all vertices.
options.feedback: Queue order and stack order are equally valid for reachability. The same forward/reverse condition proves universal contact with the same resource bounds.

options.text: Traverse outgoing edges from 0 and return true if all vertices are discovered.
options.feedback: In Example 2, 0 reaches both vertices, but 1 cannot reach 0. Reachability from a single source does not prove the reverse direction.

options.text: Run a complete matrix-based reachability traversal from every start and return true only if each reaches every vertex.
options.feedback: This checks the exact contract for all inputs. However, one forward and one reverse traversal suffice; searching from every source repeats matrix scans unnecessarily.

feedback.reason: Universal directed reachability can be proved through one hub only when both directions to that hub are established. The input representation determines the neighbor-scan cost.
details: Allocate visited arrays and one explicit stack. Mark and push vertex 0. Pop each reached u and scan every column v in row u, pushing unseen v with M[u][v]=true. If some vertex is unreached, return false. Reset visited and repeat from 0, now scanning M[v][u] for every v. Return whether this reverse traversal reaches all vertices.

Reachability from vertex zero in both the original and transpose directions proves mutual reachability through zero. A matrix traversal scans absent entries too; few true edges do not turn those row/column scans into sparse-list work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze matrix-two-searches, using iterative stack traversals as revealed. V is the matrix dimension. Preallocate V visited entries and a V-slot stack; reuse them between searches. Mark before pushing, scan V matrix cells for each popped vertex, and include array initialization/reset. Direct indexing and stack operations are constant time. Do not transpose or copy the matrix or build lists. Exclude input and scalar output; include all working storage. No hashing, recursion, amortized growth or shifting. Use the worst case in which both traversals reach all vertices.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space, where E is the number of true matrix cells

feedback.reason: Two traversals can each scan V cells for each reached vertex.
details: The option “O(V²) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: each of two traversals can scan V cells for each of V vertices, even when few matrix entries are true. Visited and stack storage are O(V). The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space, where E is the number of true matrix cells” incorrectly treats matrix neighbor enumeration as adjacency-list enumeration; even a sparse matrix requires scanning absent entries in this implementation. The option “O(V²) time, O(V²) auxiliary space” counts a matrix copy that is not made. The option “O(V³) time, O(V) auxiliary space” describes running a full matrix search from every source instead of only twice.
